# Help Scout Beacon / AI and the EU AI Act: your disclosure duty, not Help Scout's

If your website runs **Help Scout Beacon / AI**, visitors chatting with it are interacting with an AI system — and from **2 August 2026**, Article 50(1) of the EU AI Act requires them to be told so, clearly, before the conversation starts. Help scout provides the tool; **you**, the deployer, carry the legal duty.

## Why Help Scout Beacon / AI is squarely in scope

Beacon's AI answers and Docs suggestions serve visitors before agents. That is precisely the situation Article 50 was written for: a person interacting with software that talks back like a person. Our detection database fingerprints Help Scout Beacon / AI on a page in seconds — exposure level: **medium** — and a regulator (or a competitor) can run the same check.

## What the law expects on your site

- A clear, visible notice that the visitor is interacting with an AI system — at first contact, not buried in terms.
- In place wherever the interaction happens (chat widget, embedded messenger, voice interface).
- Honest wording: a human name on the bot doesn't remove the duty; it increases the risk.

## The mistakes to avoid

- Assuming Help Scout's branding or a robot avatar counts as disclosure — it doesn't, unless it clearly informs the user they're talking to AI.
- Relying on the vendor's own compliance — Article 50 duties sit with the deployer.
- Waiting for the "2027 delay" — that was the high-risk rulebook, not Article 50. [What actually got delayed →](/answers/digital-omnibus-ai-act-delay)
